utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-98-32-T, the Prosecutor versus Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Bauer.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness VG78. Please sit back and relax.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Don't invite them to sit too far back, because we have to hear them.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Going back to the afternoon hours of the 14th of June, 1992, you told this Court that Mitar Vasiljevic singled out three men and brought them back not even an hour later. Did you see how he singled them out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Where did he stand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was in the house, he went into the house and just pointed, said, "You, you, and you," and singled them out, and they went off with him and he didn't bring them back within the hour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: You mean he did bring them back within an hour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was in front of the door and they went into the house themselves.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Do you know or do you recall what he singled them out for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember, allegedly, that they were to dig graves and to bury our dead in the village of Nezuci.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: When you saw him singling these three men out, how far away would you estimate was he from you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About five steps away, because it was all in the house, in a room.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Was there anything disguising his face at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Did you see his face?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: A couple of more questions regarding the last time you saw Mitar Vasiljevic that evening. You said that you exited one house to go to another one, and you told us that the outside was lit. Were there any lights inside the house you stayed in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Just outside.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: When you exited the first house, did you take any of your belongings along?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Everything stayed in the house that we were in.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Why didn't you take them along?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what they ordered, that we should leave our things so that they could search them for weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Did you exit all together or individually?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. One by one, one after the other.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: You told this Court that Mitar Vasiljevic was standing closer to the house where you were supposed to be led into than the one which you were in. How far away would you estimate was it from the shed to the point where he was standing when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 20 steps away; 10, 20.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: You said he was walking around and watching people going from one house to the other. At the time you recognised him, did he stand still or was he walking?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Walking.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Was there anything covering his face at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Was he still armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Was there any doubt in your mind that the man you recognised as Mitar Vasiljevic that night was the same man you saw during the day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I recognised him straight away. I saw it was him straight away, looking at his profile. I didn't see him very well, but walking up and down, I recognised him.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: You said that VG101 and you escaped. When did you make the decision to escape, meaning spontaneously on the spot or earlier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. When we were in the house, a person told us that they had raped her and that they had abused her and that our turn would come, and that's why we tried to escape.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: You said a person told you. Could you tell the Court which person that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember the first and last name, but I know that she sat together with us, and that's what she told us.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Who ran to the shed first, VG101 or you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was already there at the end -- by the shed near the house. I just heard a rustling noise nearby, and I saw VG101 and I went after her, and that's how we escaped together down by the creek.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Did you turn towards the town downstream of the creek or upwards of the creek?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not towards town but along the creek, away from town. The direction was away from town.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Did you hear or see anything else coming from the direction of the house that you just escaped from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We went further away and reached a village called "Babin Potok." We arrived the next day, not that evening but the following day, at around 5.00, going through the woods.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to go into a short private session for the introduction of a document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: What is it, a photo?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Well, it has a number of names which would identify this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Very well, then. Private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: And the document is marked P68.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You mean it's already an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: It is not an exhibit. It is only a document marked as P68.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: And could I please tender this exhibit as P68?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We're now in public session. Any objection to that, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Exhibit P68, and it is under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Thank you, VG78. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, madam.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: On the 14th of June, 1992, you started out from your village; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you remember what day of the week it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you remember, at the place called "Greben," that you met and were accompanied for a time by a Serb?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: If I were to tell you the name, "Mico Lipovac," does that ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: During your journey to Visegrad, did anybody from your column from Koritnik give up and decide not to go further?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't remember anybody staying behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Your sister went with you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Were you ever separated throughout that journey?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So you went together all the time and you were together at all the places that you spoke about; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you came to Visegrad and came up to the hotel that you refer to as the new hotel --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: -- who did you see first of the Serbs who were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognised Mitar Vasiljevic and several -- and there were several others. I knew them by sight, but I didn't know who they were exactly. I didn't know their first and last names.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So he was already in front of the hotel when you appeared with the group from Koritnik, is that right, and he was with some other people as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you remember that in 1995 you gave a statement in Visoko to the MUP of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: That was at the beginning of the year sometime, less than three years after the event; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you tell them the whole truth about what had happened that day on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I talked about it. There wasn't much time, and as the days went by and the years went by, you can't remember everything, you know, what happened and how it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes. As you gave the statement at the beginning of 1995, and you yourself state that your memory and recollections were better then than they were later on -- would you say that was true? Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I had the same recollection. Maybe I didn't remember all the details and points, but I put them in the second statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. You say -- what you're saying is that in the second statement that you gave to the investigators, you added something that you had recollected later on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, because I couldn't think of everything at the time, couldn't remember everything at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What I'm asking you now is: What you remembered at the time and recounted was fresh in your mind, and you were probably telling the truth about what had happened at that time; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I told the truth in the first statement and I told the truth in the second statement, as far as I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you recall having said in the first statement which you gave in January 1995, in Visoko, that, and I quote: "In front of the Red Cross, in the Mahala settlement, Mitar took us off, whose surname I don't know, but he lived in the village of Pozdercici, and he was with two other Chetniks at the time."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know that he was from Prelovo. Whether he lived there or not, or somewhere in town, I don't know, but I did know him and I knew his face. He was well known to me. I would see him around town. He would be a passerby that I would recognise.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: But let me remind you. You said on the occasion: "A certain Mitar," to quote you, "whose surname I do not know." So in 1995 you stated that you did not know his surname, whereas in your later statement, in the subsequent statement, given after he was arrested, you gave us the surname Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because I couldn't remember his surname, and then I remembered what his surname was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, you said -- the name you gave at the MUP at the time was just Mitar, because you couldn't recall his surname; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: But I assume that you knew what he looked like, because much less time had elapsed. Did you hear my question, madam?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Could you repeat it, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You couldn't remember the surname, but I assume you knew what he looked like very well, judging by your description, because it was only two and a half years after the event; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you remember that on that occasion, you said that Mitar, without a surname, you say, and I quote: "Mitar was wearing a civilian dress with a sajkaca or cap on his head, whereas his escorts, the people with him, had camouflage uniforms on and were armed with rifles."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I remembered later on, I remembered that he had a hat and coat on. First of all, I thought he had a hat and coat on, and then I thought he -- remembered he had a camouflage uniform on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you remember having made this statement, regardless of the fact that you remembered later details for the second statement? Is this what you said to the MUP in 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember exactly. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: If we were to show you the statement, could you take a look at the statement to see if it is indeed your own statement with your signature at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can have a look.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You said a moment ago that you remembered later that he was wearing a camouflage uniform. Do you mean -- are you referring to the statement you gave to the investigator of The Hague Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I gave a statement then and said that he was wearing a coat and hat on his head and that he had the multicoloured uniform type of clothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: That was the statement you gave this year, at the beginning of this year; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What would you say was correct? Was he wearing civilian clothing with a sajkaca or a type of hat on his head, as you said in 1995, or was he wearing a coat with a multicoloured uniform and hat, as you stated this year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: With a coat and hat on his head and a uniformed suit, multicoloured.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you remember, when you testified here before the Court at the beginning, having stated that he had an SMB, that is, an olive-grey uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So according to you, he was wearing a multicoloured uniform or what is commonly referred to as a camouflage uniform; is that what you had in mind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the camouflage multicoloured clothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can you remember today, as regards the statement that you gave to MUP in 1995, what you stated about the event itself on that night, the event involving the fire and the killing of your fellow villagers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may have left out some things and perhaps added something else here, but I don't think that there is any significant difference between the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I will try to remind you of that statement to refresh your memory, because there is a difference concerning the fact that in that statement concerning the event when you and your sister fled, you failed to mention the presence of Mitar, whom on that day you had seen and told us about what he was doing. I will quote your statement, and I should like you to confirm whether that indeed was your statement and whether it was correct. You said that: "In the evening, around 23.30, Milan Lukic arrived in the house wearing a camouflage uniform. I know him from the primary school, and I heard that before the aggression he had worked in Obrenovac. He was accompanied by five or six armed Chetniks, including a young boy aged 15 who provoked us. And when a child started to cry, he took out a knife and he said, 'Bring it over so that I can slaughter him.' Lukic ordered us to go over to the adjacent house and leave our belongings there because allegedly they wanted to inspect our belongings and search them for weapons. So one by one we went to this other house, which was some 20 metres away from this one. As we were crossing over, me and my sister escaped and hid behind a shed." And then you went on to enumerate the persons who were with you, but you didn't mention that on that night you saw -- or you never mentioned the presence of the man whom you referred to as "Mitar," that is, the same person whom you had seen in front of the hotel that afternoon.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I didn't state that Milan Lukic entered the house that particular night because I didn't see him. I don't know whether he was outside. But as for Mitar Vasiljevic, I saw him in front of the door as I was trying to escape. I saw his profile and I recognised him as being Mitar Vasiljevic. As for Milan Lukic, he did not go into the house that particular night, but in the morning. As for this young boy whom they wanted to slaughter, that is true, but that happened during the day, not during the night. That is what I stated, as far as I can remember now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What was it that happened during the day, according to you? Could you please repeat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That happened around 1.00 or 2.00 p.m., when Mitar [as interpreted] Lukic took out a knife to slaughter a young boy. But Milan Lukic did not slaughter him but he grabbed him, and that is what I remember very well. It was not in the evening that Milan Lukic arrived in the house, because that night there was no light in the house. There was only some light outside the house. And we were leaving the house one by one at that time. And that is, I believe, what I stated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Just a moment, Mr. Domazet. Madam, there's a problem when the two of you, counsel and yourself, are speaking the same language. The interpretation of your answers into the English and French language for us is difficult where you answer the question straight away. If you pause slightly before you answer a question, the interpreters will be able to keep up with you. So will you please pause before you answer Mr. Domazet's questions. Yes, Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do I understand you, madam, when you say that Milan Lukic never entered the house in the evening? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I never saw him, but he did come into the house around 1.00 or 2.00 p.m. But I was so afraid, I didn't dare look at the clock, so I didn't know when people were coming in or going out. But he personally came into the house. He wanted us to give him gold and money. He told us that if we didn't give him those, that he would cut off fingers or ears and things like that. So we gave him the gold and the money, and they took everything away.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes. But that took place in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: However, your statement concerned the event which took place in the evening, the event involving the whole group which was made to go from one house to another house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not talking about the event which took place in the afternoon hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Would you please let me finish, madam, and then proceed with your question [as interpreted]. You stated that in the evening, around 11.30, that Milan Lukic came, wearing a camouflage uniform, together with five or six other uniformed Chetniks wearing camouflage uniforms and weapons, and you stated that the group included a young man, age 15, who provoked you in the way that I described a moment ago. But you said now that that was what Lukic did in the afternoon. So you were describing the event which took place in the evening and everything else that took place at that time. Except for Milan Lukic and this young Chetnik, you didn't recognise anyone else. In particular, you didn't say that the individual whom you had seen on that day as being Mitar, that he was there together with them on that night. So that is the difference that I'm talking about in your statements. Could you give us an explanation for that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I was leaving the house when they came to take us over to the second house, he was standing in front of the door with a man with a moustache whom I didn't know. And as people were moving towards this other house, they were following them, they were escorting them, and there was a smaller group of us who remained in the first house. And it was at that moment that I managed to escape. And I recognised him. I saw him standing together with Milan and others. But I didn't see him in front of the door as I was going -- as I was getting out of the house, I didn't see that. I just saw an individual with a moustache and a rifle. And at that time, we were leaving the house one by one. We were not -- we didn't leave the house together, but one after the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that, madam. I understand that your testimony is that you did not see him in front of the house. However, in the statement that you gave to the MUP, while describing this particular event, it seems that you didn't see him at all at that time. And my question is: Why didn't you mention him when you gave that statement, particularly in view of the fact that your memory was much more fresh at that time than later on, than after his arrest?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was difficult for me to remember everything. The taking of the statement didn't last very long, some 10 or 15 minutes, and it happened in 1995 and it was impossible for me to remember everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Would you be able to mark the spot where you, as you told us today, saw the individual whom you identified as Mitar Vasiljevic, on the photograph, indicating the relevant location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can have a look at the photograph, but it happened a long time ago. A lot of things have changed. I'm not sure I would be able to recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your permission, I should like to show the witness the photograph which is in evidence. It is a Prosecution exhibit, and some witnesses have already used this photograph in their evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It may be that we can get a clean copy of it. Is there one available, Ms. Bauer? What's the number of it?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: What's the number of it, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: 17.3. Well, the witness is being shown a clean copy of it, so that you had better mark it, and it will be put on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Do you require black and white copies? I have more of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes. Yours is better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The colour on the ELMO has gone right out today. They've all got green roofs. You proceed, Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Madam, do you recognise the photograph, indicating the house where you were and the house where you were taken to, and could you indicate the two on the ELMO? First of all, the house where you were on that night.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't remember this. I mean, it was all so long ago. But I think that it would have been the one without the roof, and then we went over there to Adem's house, I believe it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you recognise the house where you were up until the time when Milan Lukic came with his group and made you go over to this other house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this one here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Could you indicate with the pointer on the ELMO so that everybody can see.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was this one, this house here, that they were crossing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Very well. Would you please mark it with number "1." Could you mark the house with number "1" and circle it. You can put it on the house, yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And could you now identify the house where you were on that night.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: If that is the house in question, would you please mark it with number "2."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Could you now mark the location where you said you had seen the individual whom you identified as Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. I just cannot find my bearings here. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Could you tell us what was the distance between that individual and the house that you marked with number "1" at the moment when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I didn't hear your question. I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can you remember how far that individual was from the house which you marked with number "1," the Omeragic house, at the moment you saw him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was standing in front of the door of that house, but I don't remember exactly how far it was. I didn't measure the distance. I don't know. He was next to this other house, and that is where I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Could you see the spot where you and your sister hid when you escaped on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, we left the house --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Could you please put it back on the ELMO and indicate it there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a shed here, and it was from this side of the house that we went and headed towards the creek, and from there we went on down towards the town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet, there's a problem every time you ask the witness to point to something on the photograph. She leans right over and then loses the distortion of her face. So the audiovisual director is very concerned that, if we can, we should ask her to mark things whilst the photograph is in front of her, but then she can show it to you with the pointer once it's been put back onto the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Madam, would you please take the photograph and put it in front of you. And would you now look carefully at the photograph to see whether you can see the spot where you and your sister were hiding. And if you can please mark that spot, if you can, with number "3" and encircle it. But please do not move from your spot here, and then you will give the marked photograph to the usher.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember very well that there was a creek there, but I was so afraid. I don't know exactly where it was that we were hiding, because we left this spot here and headed off towards the town. But the fear was so great. We were trying to leave the place, leave this hellish place as soon as possible. It's not that we were hiding there. We left the place immediately and went further.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes. You moved on from there. But as far as I can understand, your sister and yourself at one point in time took shelter behind a shed and that you were able to see some individuals there and that it was after that that you escaped.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember that. After we escaped and after we reached the creek, I no longer saw anyone. That is what I believe I stated. We jumped over some fences. I remember the fences and I remember some very high grass. We managed to reach the main road leading to Babin Potok and we spent the whole night walking around the area, around Babin Potok. We couldn't get our bearings, and it was only in the following morning that we were able to actually reach the village of Babin Potok. And we stayed there for a while, but I don't know who was there and who remained behind. I wasn't able to see what happened after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, but today you have stated that after you left the house and as you were moving along, you were able to see the profile of the person whom you identified as Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When I got out of the house and when I was near the shed, as I was about to move over to the other house, to the first house, I went back when I heard that VG101 fell down next to me, and I followed her, and that is how I escaped, so I could no longer see what was going on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The document that she has been marking, do you want that put into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I would like to tender it in evidence as an exhibit. The number "1" indicates the house to which, according to her, people were brought to -- brought from the house which she marked with number "2." There are no other markings on the photograph, since the witness is unable to provide any further details.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Any objection, Ms. Bauer?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Exhibit D3. You may proceed, Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Madam, so you have identified this person as Mitar Vasiljevic today, and you saw his profile at the moment you and your sister escaped; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as I was going towards this house where the people who were eventually burnt alive were. At that point in time, we turned off, we fled towards the creek. We tried to leave the area as quickly as possible. We didn't want to linger there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I should like to ask you a couple of questions concerning your statement that on that afternoon, that is, after you reached the first house, the individual whom you identified as Mitar Vasiljevic personally selected several people to bury some dead bodies in the village of Nezuci.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You didn't speak of that in your statements, neither in the statement that you gave to the MUP, nor in the one that you gave to the investigator. How is it that you remembered this particular detail today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I remembered this particular detail because I have been thinking about this and I've been trying to remember all of the details, and I just remembered that he came to the house and he took out three individuals from the house, and that he returned them after a while, because they personally told us after they had come back that it was Mitar Vasiljevic personally who had taken them there and that he was standing behind them as they were burying the dead. They were pale with fear, and I remember one person who started to cry. And I asked him why he was crying, what had happened, and he said, "It's terrible. I don't want to talk about it." And that's how it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Was that immediately after he had put you up in that house, as you stated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I cannot recall exactly the time. One hour or half an hour maybe. The fear was so great.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Was he accompanied by any other Serb at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were standing in front of the door, they didn't enter the house, and Milan entered the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: How many were they, the people who you said were standing in front of the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't count them. I was afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you see them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw them. There were quite a lot of them. On one occasion when I went out into the hall, I saw Milan Lukic take up a knife to slaughter Almir, and I saw that there were a lot of them walking up and down in front of the door. And I saw the boy had -- he was about 16. I was mostly in the kitchen and in the room, but I didn't go out, and that evening, before they came -- that evening, before they came to transfer us to the other house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I asked you, madam, at the point where you say Mitar Vasiljevic came into the house to select a few men to go and bury the dead. Focus on that, please. And I asked you whether there were others, and you said, yes, in front of the house. And I asked whether you had seen them. Are you now describing to us the people that you had seen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but they didn't enter the house. Only Mitar Vasiljevic entered the house. They stayed in front of the door, the entrance to the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes. But you mention Milan Lukic and a young person. Were they there then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were in front of the door, not inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you say, madam, that there were a lot of them, several of them, but that you can't say exactly how many, would you say that there were two or three of them or five or six of them? What would you say corresponded to the situation; five or six or two or three?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were about ten of them, not even five, six. There were ten.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When the person whom you have identified as Mitar Vasiljevic came back and brought the others back, was he alone or was he accompanied by the same people you mentioned a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question, really. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You said that about an hour later, the people who were taken off to bury the dead were returned and that the same person returned them whom you had identified as Mitar Vasiljevic. Now, did he come back himself alone or with a group of men you mentioned earlier on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mitar Vasiljevic personally brought them back, and they told us that the others were with them. And then they came into the house and sat down. He brought them back. They buried the dead and brought the men back.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, but what I'm asking you is this: Were they accompanied by the same group of people who were there and accompanied them when the men were taking off?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know who accompanied them when they came back. But I know that they just mentioned that Mitar Vasiljevic had taken them away and brought them back, and that there were others too, and that they stood around, guarding over them, until they had buried all the dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you say, madam, that they told us that Mitar Vasiljevic had driven them, did they tell you that that person drove them in a car? Were they taken off in a car; is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in a car. They were taken by car.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did they tell you that he personally drove them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because they were older people, they knew him well. It was the older generation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So they said that Mitar Vasiljevic had driven them away and that they knew him very well; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they knew Mitar Vasiljevic, and there was some other people with them whom they also knew. But as they were afraid, one man started to cry and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did they perhaps tell you what kind of vehicle it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you remember that on that day, while you were still in front of the new hotel in Visegrad, that Serb policemen who were there singled out some people also to take them to bury some dead?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. Do you mean in front of the hotel?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes. While you were in front of the new hotel in Visegrad, before you set off for the Mahala.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I remember is that a man was taken off to the bridge. There was a dog and they asked whose it was, and he said it was his, and they ordered him to take the dog away and throw him over the bridge. But I don't remember that they singled anybody out. I don't remember that. All I remember is the incident with the dog.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So you don't remember that while standing in front of the new hotel, that they singled out anybody then, singled out people to bury the dead; you don't remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I don't. That happened in the Mahala, when we came to the house, but not in front of the new hotel, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Are you sure that the people didn't go back up there and that they had left from the new hotel to the Nezuci place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They personally came back to the house, the ones that went to bury the dead in Nezuci, in the village of Nezuci. I personally saw them come to the house, come inside and sit down.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, but my question is: Are you sure that they left from that house and not perhaps from the new hotel in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sure. I'm sure they went from that house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you started out towards the Mahala, who escorted you, if anybody?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mitar Vasiljevic and the people who were with him came in front of the door and we were put up in two houses. In one house there was Jusuf Memic and the Delija family. Ajnija was her name. We were there in two houses. I don't remember her husband's name. The third house was owned by a man called Adem. But mostly we were in Jusuf Memic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, but what I'm asking you is this: Mitar Vasiljevic and some others accompanied you throughout the trip from the hotel to those houses; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was accompanied by two men, not more. There were two of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did they walk behind you, in front of you, or beside you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were beside us, in front of us, behind us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Let me just remind you of a portion of your statement given to the OTP investigator. You described the event in the following way: You said that at the moment you arrived, the last buses had left Visegrad, that, "There were policemen, Serb policemen, in the square who were discussing what to do with us. Some of them suggested that we should be sent to the Bikavac hotel; others suggested that we should go to the Mahala district, where there were lots of empty Muslim houses. The discussion ended by them taking a decision that we should go to the Mahala settlement on foot and to Pionirska Street. That's what they decided. Nobody directed us or took us to the settlement itself. However, we all knew where that street was, and we hurried because it was already raining and we were drenched and we wanted to change our clothes. We went into an empty house in the street. I heard someone mention the name of the owner of the house, but I don't remember the name, unfortunately." Do you remember having said that in the statement you gave at the beginning of this year to the OTP investigator?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Is that statement different to your statement today, your testimony today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is a little different, but I couldn't remember, and I said a moment ago that I recalled what happened and that we did not come to the Mahala district in front of Jusuf Memic's house alone. I remember them saying, "You can go into any of the houses, because they're all empty, all Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the Muslim houses." But the buses had already left. We were to arrive there by 12.00 and to go to Kladanj. We left home at 6.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you recognise what I quoted to be the statement you gave to the OTP investigator?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What I have just read out from your statement to the investigator, do you acknowledge that you did indeed tell the OTP investigator what I read out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that we were escorted to the Mahala.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Had you said that, they would probably have recorded it in your statement, because the statement was read back to you and you signed it. But it says here that nobody directed you, that nobody escorted or accompanied you, and that you yourselves went off alone and went into one of the empty houses.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I said that I couldn't remember everything, all the details, until I sat down to think about it, and then I started remembering.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can I take your answer to mean that you did not recollect that in January this year when you gave the statement to the investigator, but that you have since remembered it now, that you remembered it and testified to it now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: In the statement you gave to the investigator, after describing how you entered the two houses and where you all where, you said: "Then Mitar Vasiljevic and four Serbs came to the house, and [redacted] [redacted], was handed a message from them. It was a piece of paper with several sentences written on it." Is that correct or is it correct that Mitar Vasiljevic came with you, as you describe, and told you which house to go into?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He told us which house to go into, and first he singled out these three people. And then half an hour or an hour later, 30 minutes perhaps, I heard from a woman. I heard her saying, "Mitar Vasiljevic is asking somebody to come out and give a piece of paper for security, for safety reasons," and if anybody were to turn up, we were to show this piece of paper or to call him. I didn't see this piece of paper. Whether Osman went out or Meho, I can't remember. I don't remember who went out to collect this piece of paper, but someone did, and Mitar gave that person this piece of paper and said that if anybody came to mistreat us, we should just contact him and there would be no problem. That's what I remember happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So others told you about that, the other people who were with you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: They said that Mitar had given one of them a piece of paper like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: But you didn't actually see this taking place, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You said today that a person slapped someone. Can you be more specific and describe that incident for us, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was in front of the hotel. He slapped a person. She had said something. And she wasn't quite normal. I don't remember what she said, but he came up to her and slapped her. And her mother said to her [as interpreted], "Don't do that. She doesn't know what she is doing." He said, "What do you mean she doesn't know what she is doing?" He added something else, but I couldn't understand what he was saying. But that's what I heard and that's what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So this took place in front of the hotel, did it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And the person who did that you have said was Mitar Vasiljevic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: That person, when you saw them the first time, in addition to your description of the events, was there any characteristic trait that you noticed on that person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He was wearing a hat and coat and that uniform type of multicoloured clothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did he have a moustache or a beard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you happen to hear anybody who was also called Mitar in Visegrad, anybody else whose name was Mitar in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You don't remember that other people said that there was a person called Mitar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: The event you have just described, that is to say, the slapping of this child in front of the hotel, you never described that event either in your statement to the investigator or to the MUP.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, but I didn't say "child." I said it was a woman, a female person. She was about 35 years old, this female.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Very well. Maybe I misunderstood you. You said that she was a little retarded, so I took it to be a child. But anyway, you don't make any mention of that fact either to the investigator or the MUP; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can you tell us why, how come you didn't remember that incident earlier and recount it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I did remember it, but we didn't have time to go into all that. I didn't have time to recount all that. I didn't have two, three, four hours. It was always for a brief space of time. I would discuss it briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: In the place where you lived this year and last year, where you've been living, did you have occasion to see on television the arrest of Mitar Vasiljevic? Did you learn that he had been arrested and was in The Hague on television?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see him on television, but I heard about it, but I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you watch television at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: On Bosnia-Herzegovina television, is there a programme which is called "The Hague Chronicle" once a week?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't have time to watch it. I'm always working outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So you claim that you have never seen that programme, nor that you ever saw him on the television screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember seeing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Were there articles written about it in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know, I don't remember. I don't buy newspapers and I don't read newspapers because I live in the village. I don't work in a firm or company. I don't go to work and buy a newspaper on my way to work and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Well, can you tell me how you came to learn of his arrest and when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I heard of it. I don't know exactly when I heard about it. And I learned about it when the people from The Hague Tribunal came for me to give a statement to them. I gave my statement, and then -- and from that time onwards, I knew that he had been captured.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes. But you gave your statement in January this year, and he was arrested a long time ago, a year ago. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you remember what I read to you a moment ago: that you told the OTP investigators that in front of the hotel, Serb policemen and not the individual you identified as Mitar Vasiljevic spoke about whether -- discussed whether you should go to Bikavac or Mahala?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was the Serb police. As far as I remember, that's what I said. And Mitar Vasiljevic was also there with his group of men, the group of men he led, him, Mitar Vasiljevic. But, yes, the Serb police were there too, but I didn't know any of them. I knew them by sight, of course, yes, but I knew -- but I didn't know their names, first and last names.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you say you didn't know their first and last names, whom do you mean; the Serb policemen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I mean the Serb policemen's names.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: My question was whether what you said in your statement is correct, that is to say, that they discussed this point with you, with the group, whether you should go to Bikavac or Mahala, that they were discussing this and not the person whom you identified today as Mitar Vasiljevic. You don't mention him then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, them and Mitar Vasiljevic, they were discussing this point amongst themselves, discussing where to send us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Was that before or after what you said Mitar spoke about on that occasion? Was it before, after, or at the same time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As soon as we came to the hotel, they were discussing this. They said that the buses had left, that we didn't have anywhere to go, and where could we spend the night, because we were first in order the next morning to go. That's what they were saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, that's what you said then. But you said that you yourselves decided to go to the Mahala and that you yourselves went off in the direction of Mahala.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I couldn't remember at the time. But since then, I've remembered, so that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Madam, would you take a look at the January 1995 statement that you gave to the Security Services Centre in Visoko. Is that your statement, in fact, and is it your signature on your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'll take a look, gladly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I have the witness shown that statement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Do we have it?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, I think that you have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I don't. I think the OTP has got it, if anybody's got it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Sorry, I would have to check. I have an English copy, but I'll check whether I have a B/C/S copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Does it have a number?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: A number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, a number.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: It doesn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: All right. Then we won't have it. Are you able to identify that by any description, a date or something?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the date. It is mine; that is to say, the signature is mine, the name and surname.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Ms. Bauer, does it have a date?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Yes. It is dated the 24th of January, 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I suggest that the witness reads through the statement carefully. As we're coming up to a break, perhaps it would be a good idea to do this during the break, she can do this during the break, and then she can tell us, when we reconvene, whether it is indeed the statement she gave and signed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: She's already said it's got her signature on it. But if you want her to check it through, that's all right. Have you got something else to go on with until we adjourn?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps, Your Honour, she could look through the statement, read through it during the break, and then afterwards she could tell us whether there is anything that is not correct in the statement and why it is in the statement if that is so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Domazet, that, if I may say so, is not a very satisfactory way of cross-examination. If you want to take her to a particular part of it, by all means do so. It's almost 11.00, so we'll give her the opportunity of reading it. But I don't think that that's going to help us very much unless you direct her attention to particular matters that you want to have determined either to have been true or untrue. We'll adjourn now. We'll resume at 11.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to read this statement during the break?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: This is your statement that you gave and that you signed on the 24th of January, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you notice the part where you speak about having seen for the first time, in front of the Red Cross building, the person by the name of Mitar, whose last name you said you did not know, who was dressed in civilian clothes with a sajkaca hat on his head and that he was unarmed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is stated here in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Could you tell us -- could you tell the Court the difference between sajkaca, a Serbian traditional hat, and a regular hat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A regular -- he had a very large hat on his head, whereas a sajkaca, as far as I remember, is closer to the head and it has something on the front part, some kind of sign.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Would it be correct for me to say that sajkaca doesn't have any rim, unlike a hat, which does have a rim, and the hat, the particular hat that you described, had an especially large rim?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. He had a very large hat with a rim.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Sajkaca is a typical cap, a typical hat usually worn by Serbs and not Muslims; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And sajkaca does not have a rim at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Were you able to notice that in your statement, apart from the place where you describe Mitar as wearing civilian clothes and a sajkaca, no weapons at all, you also mentioned that a certain Meho from Sase gave him a certificate? That is, apart from these two incidents, you made no mention of him in that particular statement, including the event which took place in Pionirska Street on that night; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did mention Meho. He continued along the way with us. He joined us in his village. He was also in the house, but I didn't tell his name in this list that I made because I didn't know his surname then. But I think that his surname is Jasarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, but the reason I mentioned this was because, in your statement, the person referred to as Mitar is mentioned only on these two occasions, that is, when you saw him wearing a sajkaca, as you have described, and also when you speak about a certain Meho from Sase, to whom he allegedly gave some kind of certificate. So apart from these two instances, you make no mention of him at all in your statement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You have also described in that statement an event which -- that is, the other event which took place at around 11.30, when you and your sister escaped; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You have testified today that your sister was with you throughout that period of time, that is, from the beginning of the journey until the end; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you ever separate at any point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: According to what you can remember, she was with you all the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, also in the house where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And she went with you towards the house and she also left the house with you when you escaped?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So if I understand you correctly, your sister was also able to see and hear whatever you were able to see and hear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. She may have seen something that I didn't see at a particular point in time, but more or less I think that throughout that period of time, from the house up to the hotel, and when at Mahala and onwards, we more or less saw the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did your sister also give a statement to the MUP of Bosnia and Herzegovina before she gave a statement to investigators of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because I lived in Visoko and she didn't live there at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: She never told you anything about having given any other statement concerning these events to some other authority?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, she did, but to some ordinary people, some teachers or other individuals who were involved in this. I remember a man from Zenica who questioned her about it. But I didn't give a statement at that time at all. But I don't exactly remember to whom she gave a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Was that an individual who was writing a book about those events or an investigator from the MUP?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think he was an investigator from the MUP. I think that he was just an ordinary man. I don't -- I don't know. I can't remember. It was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you testified today about the fact that he was wearing a very large hat which was different from this sajkaca type of hat, can you remember what colour it was; the hat, that is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No -- I mean, yes, the hat. I thought you were referring to a sajkaca. I think that the hat was grey, unicoloured.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You described in detail what he was wearing. You didn't tell us - you may have not noticed - what he was wearing on his feet, what kind of footwear he was wearing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So you don't remember what kind of footwear he was wearing, whether he was barefoot or whether he had something else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Before the time when you and your sister decided to leave the column and try to escape, were you able to have a good view of the house where people were being taken to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, just a little.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: In the statement that you made in January this year to the investigator of the Prosecution, you said that you had seen armed men in front of the house and on the sides of the house and that there was no entrance door to that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because other people told me that there was no actual door, that there was only a curtain hanging there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So you -- this is what you stated to the investigator on the basis of what other people had told you; it is not something that you personally saw?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't come close, I didn't go into the house, so I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you spoke about the event involving plunder and seizure of belongings from you and others in which Milan Lukic took part, you told the Court that it happened during the day, shortly after Mitar Vasiljevic had left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: In the statement you gave to the investigator, you said it was dark, that it was dark in the house, and that there were only some street lights outside. So what is true; can you remember now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that it was still day, 2.00 or 3.00 p.m., maybe even 4.00 p.m., when Milan Lukic came to the house and seized our money and our gold.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So since it was in the month of June, it could not have been dark; it was still daylight?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, one could see outside. It was not dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you remember having stated that to the investigator, that is, that you stated to the investigator that it was dark and that street lights were on? Do you remember having said that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, yes. But when Milan Lukic came to the house to take our money and our gold, it was still daylight.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Let me just quote this very short portion from your statement, and will you please confirm whether this is what you stated and if you Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. remember that: "When it became dark, Milan Lukic appeared in the house. We were inside, there was no electricity, and I believe that street lights were already on. Members of his group were in front of his house. They came in two cars. I didn't see the cars, but that is what I was told. We gathered in the basement of the house."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, maybe I -- my memory didn't serve me right at that time. As far as I can remember now, it was still daylight. One could see outside. And when we left the house, it was dark, it was in the evening. There was no light in the house at that time, but I remember that the street was lit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no further questions for the witness, except that I would like to make an agreement with the Prosecution as to certain differences in statements, certain discrepancies concerning the statement given to the investigator, so that we do not tender this into evidence, if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You already have that, to a very large extent, haven't you? Is there something that the witness didn't agree with? It's only where the witness has not agreed that there is something different in the statement. My recollection, which may prove to be faulty when the transcript is read, is that the witness in each case agreed that she had not included the particular matter or had agreed that she had included the particular matter in her previous statements.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters have not been provided with the relevant statement, so what you have heard was just a simultaneous interpretation of what the counsel quotes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, one thing is the statement that she gave to the MUP in 1995, where we clarified the problem. However, the statement which was given to the investigator contains certain discrepancies concerning some, in my opinion, very crucial things. In the statement that she made to the investigator, from that statement one can conclude that she didn't at all see the person whom she identified as Mitar in front of the hotel. So in the statement given to the investigator, she only referred to Serb policemen who told her where to go and that after that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Please don't repeat it all. We've heard it at least twice during the cross-examination already. We know the point you've made. I've suggested to you that the witness has agreed that she did not include those matters in the statements. The matter that she did say she agreed she included was the reference to or the description of the hat that the man was wearing. Now, why is there any need to go through this procedure if you've already got an agreement from the witness that those discrepancies arise? I pointed out to you that this procedure is available and it should be followed where the witness does not agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree, Your Honour, if that's what she has agreed with. However, it seems to me that the witness did not agree that this is not contained in the statement given to the investigator. If that is indeed correct, then of course there's no need for me to repeat it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, then, may I suggest to you you wait until you see the transcript. If it's not there, then you raise it with the Prosecution. But it has probably taken longer to debate this with you than it would have taken to do it, but I'm trying to stop this happening in every case. Where the witness does agree, there is no need to obtain the Prosecution's acceptance. You wait until you've seen the transcript. If there's something there that you say has not been agreed, then it can be agreed. May I also draw your attention to this: that if you want to cross-examine the witnesses on their statements, as I think has been your practice, it is best to ensure that the interpreters have copies of the statements so that they can follow them. It's always easier for them to ensure that they are using the same language as is in the statement. They should be supplied, of course, by the Prosecution in any event, as I understand it. But just would you please make certain that the interpreters do have the statements before you cross-examine on them. Now, is that the end of your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Bauer, that is something which the Prosecution should have done. They should have supplied a whole set of these to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: My understanding is that probably the English versions from the OTP statements have been supplied but not the copy of the MUP statement, because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Oh, I see. All right, then. Now, do you want to re-examine?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Only two short questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: VG79 [sic], have you been ever asked to provide such details about the events like you were inquired about today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: And what you told the Court today, is this the best recollection of the events that occurred on the 14th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG78 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAUER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much, madam, for coming to give evidence. That finishes your task here. We're very grateful to you for your assistance. You are now free to leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution calls its next witness, VG38.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Sir, would you please make the solemn declaration in the document which the Court usher is showing you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Sit down, please. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness 38. Before we begin, you will be here for quite some time; if you want to take off your jacket, please feel free to take off your jacket if you so desire. I'd ask that the witness be shown the pseudonym sheet, which is document number 88.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit P88 and it will be under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Witness 38, I would ask you to take a look at Exhibit P88 in front of you, and ask you, is that your name on the top line of that document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And is that your date of birth on the second line of that document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: For the purposes of concealing your identity, we will refer to you throughout the course of these proceedings as "Witness 38." I would ask you, if you need to refer to any of the witnesses listed on that document, that you please do so by referring to their number. I'd like to begin by asking you to tell us a bit about your background. The first question I would ask you is: Did you complete primary school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And where did you go to primary school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: In Visegrad. The name of the school was (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what street is that school located on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: In the neighbourhood called Mahala.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is that school across the street from the events that you are going to testify about today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: After finishing primary school, did you go to a secondary technical school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes, but that was in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what profession did you learn?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Locksmith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what is your ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: I'm a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I want to draw your attention back to 1992. How old were you at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Thirteen and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what village did you grow up in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Koritnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, I want to draw your attention to a specific day, the 15th of April of 1992. Did something happen in the village of Koritnik on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what was it that happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: We were attacked by local Serbs, our neighbours, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And where did that attack come from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: From a neighbouring village, Koritnik. We lived nearby.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were any of the villagers from Koritnik injured in that attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you able to see that some bullets had hit houses in the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
