utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you able to see whether or not bullets -- or some windows in those houses had been shot out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time that day that members or villagers from the village of Koritnik left Koritnik that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And approximately how many villagers left that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Fifty-six, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And where did those villagers go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: We went to the village of Brstanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And where is that village in relation to the village of Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: The two villages are separated by the Drina River only.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is Brstanica a Muslim village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And how did these people from Koritnik get to the village of Brstanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Well, we went to the river by ourselves, and then we crossed the river in boats.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When you arrived at Brstanica, would you describe what you saw when you arrived there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: We were met there by the Uzice Corps with trucks.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what happened in Brstanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: We were forced to leave the village, that is, the neighbouring villages surrounding the town of Visegrad, and then we were transported to the stadium.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And how were you transported to the stadium?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Some went on foot and some in trucks.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How did you yourself go to the stadium?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: In a truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When you arrived at the stadium, were there other people present in the stadium?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you approximate for the Court approximately how many people were in the stadium?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: There were about 6.000 people.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And from what you could tell, what was the majority -- what was the ethnic majority of those people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Mostly they were Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what occurred in the stadium?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: They separated military-age men.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What happened to those men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: We haven't heard anything of them ever since.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What else happened in the stadium that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: They were looking for weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And how did they look for weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: They searched us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were you yourself searched?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were the women in the crowd searched?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were the children in the crowd searched?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: All of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was anything said to the crowd at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you were allowed to leave the stadium?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Some did, some didn't, because we didn't dare go back.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You didn't dare go back where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: The village of Koritnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And so where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: We stayed at the stadium, at the Drina Hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where is the Drina Hotel in relation to the stadium?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: In the middle.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: From this point in time onward, did you ever attend school again in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How long did you stay in the Drina Hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Fifteen days.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And without telling us their names, would you tell us who you stayed there with.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: VG13, VG18 and VG084.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were there other people from Koritnik staying in the hotel at that time as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, did there come a time when members of the Uzice Corps allowed you to go and get some food?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And would you describe for the members of the Court how they allowed you to go get food.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Well, when we went to the shops, they filmed it on -- with a camera. When they didn't, they would curse and swear at us. When the cameras were off, they would curse at us and swear at us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And approximately how many times were you allowed to go and get food in this manner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Just once.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And where were the shops that you were allowed to go and get food from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Near the bus stop in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: After spending 15 days in the Drina Hotel, where did you go when you left it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: We went to the village of Koritnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you describe what you saw when you returned there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: As not everybody could go, there were some older women who stayed in Koritnik village.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And could you tell whether the house that you lived in had been damaged or looted in any way when you were away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So it was not damaged or looted; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time after you returned that you had conversations with local Serbs regarding whether or not you should remain in Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe for us the contents of those conversations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: We talked to them about a return. Allegedly we weren't allowed to be there because -- we shouldn't be there because one side would attack us, but they didn't know which side, which army.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did these types of warnings continue throughout the month of May?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And in the early part of June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I want to now draw your attention to the 13th of June. Do you recall that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And do you recall somebody from another village coming to speak to the members of your village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What was the name of this person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: I don't know his proper name, but I know his nickname.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Would you tell us that, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Ciro.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you know where this person was from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what village was this person from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Loznica.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you tell us, approximately how far away is Loznica from Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Perhaps about 15 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us what happened when this person you've referred to as "Ciro" arrived in Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Well, that we had to leave the village. They promised us buses to take us to the free territory, that is to say, to Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask you to use the words that this Ciro person used when he told you this.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: "You must leave the village because the army will attack," some foreign army; they don't know which.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe how this person was dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: He had a multicoloured uniform on.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what was the -- is this a camouflage uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what was the predominant colour in that uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Green.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And was this person, Ciro, armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, would it be fair to say that the village of Koritnik has both Muslim families and Serb families living there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you see Mr. Ciro address these warnings to any of the Serb families?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So it was only addressed to Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us approximately what time of day this occurred?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And that is in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was your mother present during this morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And approximately how long did this interaction with this person Ciro last?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Not more than 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were you able to see where Ciro went after he warned you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: He went back to where the Serbs were mostly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is that the Serb houses in Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Approximately how many Muslims were in the group with you that were warned by him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: They were elderly persons who were not up to it, five of them. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. They were not fit for service. There were about five of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I want to draw your attention to that night. Did you and your mother discuss whether you should try to leave Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At that point in time, had you heard of Muslims being killed in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you decide that night to leave Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you and your mother that night decide to leave Koritnik in the municipality of Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you pack that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe for us briefly what you packed to take with you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Mostly clothes; underwear and clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you pack any food?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you given an instruction regarding how much food to pack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you pack any photos or other family possessions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: On this night, did you think that you would be coming back or returning to Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And was a plan made or an arrangement made for the time that you would leave Koritnik the next morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Could you repeat that, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you and your mother agree that you should leave at a particular time the next morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what time was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: 7.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you gather to leave at 7.00 in the morning the next day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And where did you gather?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: In front of the shop in Koritnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were there other people there aside from yourself and your mother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Without telling us their names, can you approximate the number of people that had gathered at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Well, about 50.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say that most of these people were related to you in some way or another?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Aside from these Muslim people, was there anybody else present at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And who was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Dusan Gavrilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what is his ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: A Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you describe for us how he was dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: He didn't have a uniform on, but he was armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what was he armed with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: An automatic weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did he say anything to you and other people in the group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Allegedly the buses were supposed to transfer us to Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were there any buses in Koritnik that morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did this person you've described as Dusan, did he say anything regarding how you would get to Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: The buses were to come and get us, but as they didn't arrive, we had to go on foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And approximately what time would you estimate you departed from Koritnik that morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: About half past 7.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: This person Dusan, did he go with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes, to the village of Greben.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is Greben the next village on the way to Visegrad from Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you tell us how far away is Greben from Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: About 15 minutes on foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, this person Dusan, where exactly, where precisely did he walk in relation to the group of people that left Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: He was in front of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And you said that 50 or 60 people -- 50 to 60 people gathered at 7.00 in the morning. Did that entire group leave for Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was there a dog also in the group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did that dog belong to one of the people who was travelling down to Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, did you in fact arrive in the village of Greben that morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you describe for the Chamber what occurred after you arrived in the village of Greben.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: When we got down there, we still waited for the buses, but as they didn't show any signs of turning up, we left. A Golf car came by once. And there were two policemen there. They were wearing uniforms, and they swore at us and said, "Fuck your mothers. We'll drown you in the Drina."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did they remain in Greben, the two policemen? Did they remain there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No. They went further on towards Prelovo village.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was that up in the direction from which you had just come?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you see this person you've referred to as Dusan go anywhere when you arrived in Greben?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Dusan went to Lipovac, Milorad.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is that the name of a person: Lipovac, Milorad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you know this person from before this day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When this group from Koritnik stopped in Greben, would it be fair to say that they were in the centre of the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were you able to see the house of Lipovac, Milorad at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes. His house is right by the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And Dusan, did he enter that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you saw somebody leave that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Lipovac -- Milorad Lipovac went out.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And approximately how much time transpired between the time you saw Dusan go in and Lipovac Milorad come out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Perhaps three minutes. It was just in passing, because we were going down to Greben, towards the main road towards Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What did Milorad Lipovac do after he left the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: He took us over and took us off in the direction of Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did he say anything to you and other members of the group before he left for Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: He just said, "The buses are due to arrive, but since they didn't arrive, we have to walk."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did he say what would happen to you when you arrived in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Allegedly that we would be transported to Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Approximately how long did you remain in Greben in total?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Just about half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: After you left Greben, what would be the next village that the group headed towards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Sase.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you arrive at Sase?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you approximate for us how long it took to get from Greben to Sase?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Whereas there was some elderly women and women with children, about an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when the group arrived at the intersection of the road you were travelling on and the road that goes up to the Vilina Vlas Hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask you to describe to the Chamber what you observed at that intersection.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: There was a sort of checkpoint there. There were five people in camouflage uniforms, and they were armed with automatic weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what, if anything, happened at that checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No, nothing happened there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: On the road between Greben and Sase, did you pass by houses belonging to Serb people on the road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes, we did. Along the road, there was a lot of swearing from the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: On the road between Greben and Sase, did you see a bus travelling on that road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And was the bus travelling to Visegrad or from Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: To Visegrad, but the bus was transporting Muslims from the neighbouring village of Vlahovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And was the bus full?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How many buses did you see that morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Three buses passed by.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you able to tell who was in the other buses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: People from the village of Vlahovici as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, what would be the next village going from Vlahovici to Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Kosovo Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And before you left for the village of Kosovo Polje, did any people from the village of Sase join this group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Approximately how many?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: About 10, 10 to 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you able to learn what their intention was in going to Visegrad that morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Well, I learned that they were allegedly going to transport us to Zenica because we weren't safe in those villages. That's what was allegedly said.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Approximately how long did it take you to reach Kosovo Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Not longer than 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, would it be fair to say that, in Kosovo Polje, the population is made up of both Muslim families and Serb families?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And do the Muslim families in Kosovo Polje live in a particular area of Kosovo Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Could you repeat that, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The Muslim families living in Kosovo Polje, did they at that time live in a particular area of Kosovo Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you describe, in relation to the road that you were travelling on, where those Muslim families lived.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Moving from Koritnik to Visegrad, the Muslims lived on the right-hand side and the Serbs lived on the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where is the Drina at this point; which side of the road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Below the road, that is to say, on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I just want to ask you a few questions to help orient us regarding this trip. Would it be fair to say that -- or let me ask you this: Koritnik is on which bank of the Drina; the western bank or the eastern bank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Eastern.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And is that commonly referred to as "the right bank" by people living in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, travelling from Koritnik to the town centre of Visegrad, would it be necessary to cross the Drina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So that they are on the same side of the Drina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, near the centre of Visegrad, is there another river that joins up with the Drina River?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes, the River Rzav.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And from which direction does the River Rzav come from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: From the direction of --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Let me ask the question in another way. Travelling from Koritnik to the centre of Visegrad, would the group have had to have crossed the Rzav River?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes. It flows from the direction of Dobrun. That's the direction of the Rzav River.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did the group cross the Rzav River that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Approximately how much time did it take for this group to travel from Kosovo Polje to this point where you're about to cross the Rzav River?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: About half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And is there a bridge crossing the Rzav River at that place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe for us where that bridge is in relation to the police station in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Going from the Pionirska valley to Visegrad, across the river, right by the Rzav bridge, on the left-hand side, is where the police station, or rather, the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And are you able to estimate what time it was when you arrived at the Rzav bridge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: About half past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Chamber what you observed at that location at that time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: When we crossed the bridge, there was a group of armed people by the MUP and there was a car there. I wasn't able to identify it. On the car, there was a machine-gun while we were crossing the Rzav bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Approximately how many people were in this group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: About five or six people.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And was this group of people within eyesight of the MUP station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were you able to see where this machine-gun was being pointed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: At us as we were crossing the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did any of these men say anything to the group as the group crossed the bridge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: They just cursed us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were any threats made?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you know where Milorad Lipovac is at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: He was in front of us, ahead of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, from the point in time where you first see him in Greben until this point in time now, has he been with the group the entire time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes, but some ten metres ahead of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: After you crossed the bridge, where did you and this group go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: We went towards the old bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And approximately how long does it take or did it take to travel from the Rzav bridge to the old bridge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Not more than 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And was Milorad Lipovac with you as you travelled to the old bridge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe for us where is the old bridge in relation to a hotel which is commonly called the new hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: To the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And approximately how far away is it from -- how far away is the hotel from the bridge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: I'm not able to tell that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you see the bridge from the front of the hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: I'm not very familiar with this new hotel. I've heard of it, but I'm not able to explain to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The dog that you mentioned, was the dog still with the group at this point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did something happen to the dog when you arrived in this area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us what happened to the dog?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Jovo Rajak was there. He's from Lijeska. And he was wearing an automatic weapon and he said, "Take this dog away. He's going to bite someone." And then he fired five bullets into him, into it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did they kill the dog, or did this person kill the dog?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What was done with the dog after it had been shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Alija Kurspahic took it away, together with Munira Kurspahic, and they threw it from the old bridge into the Drina.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When you arrived at this location, did you see Milorad Lipovac speaking with anybody?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And who did you see him speaking with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: With Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And for approximately how long did they speak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Not more than ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Court how it is you know that the person you're referring to now is Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: He used to work in Panos in the new hotel, and sometimes he would be in the Vilina Vlas Hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you have any relatives that also knew him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And without telling us the name of any relatives, can you tell us what their relationship was with Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: They were on very good terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you have a relative that also worked in one of the places that Mitar Vasiljevic worked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes. He was an intern there, a trainee.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you were shown a group of photographs of 12 different people and asked whether or not you could recognise anybody?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you recognise anybody in that group of photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: I recognised Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you do anything on that group of photographs to mark or indicate that you recognised Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes; I signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would ask to go into private session for the purposes of showing an exhibit which bears the name of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But where is it going to reveal it? It doesn't have to be shown on the ELMO, does it?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, it doesn't, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, then let's get on with it without worrying about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I would ask that the witness be shown Prosecution Exhibit 20.38.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Witness 38, Prosecution Document Number 20.38 has been placed in front of you. Do you recognise what this document is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: These are photographs of criminals.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And is this the group of photographs that you were shown in connection with this case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And you said that earlier -- that you indicated one of these photographs to be that of Mitar Vasiljevic. Can you tell us the number of which photograph you identified as such?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Number 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And does this document contain your photograph? I mean - sorry - your signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would tender Prosecution Document Number 20.38 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Any objection, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. That will be Exhibit P20, VG038, and it will be under seal. Mr. Groome, are you going to try to pin down the appearance of Mr. Vasiljevic more than we have at the moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We started back at 12.00, and there was 20 minutes for something and then something else happened. But at the moment, this is left completely up in the air.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'll do that now. Before I do it, Your Honour, I just have a couple of questions to ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Would you recognise Mr. Vasiljevic if you saw him again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask you to look around the courtroom today and tell us, do you recognise anybody in this courtroom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And who do you recognise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you describe where the person you're identifying now is sitting and describe what he is wearing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: He's wearing a brown blazer, and he's sitting at the back; on the left side, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Let the record reflect --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We've agreed that he has identified the accused. "The record reflecting" is a term which means all sorts of things, but it doesn't really mean that. But I know that it's an American phrase that we hear so often here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, I want to take you back to this initial viewing of Mitar Vasiljevic. Approximately how far away were you from Mitar Vasiljevic at this particular point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Not more than five metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And are you able to tell us what you remember about what he was wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: He was wearing a large black hat on his head and a black uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And do you recall whether or not he was armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No. I mean he didn't have a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did he say anything to you and other members of the group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: He said that there were no buses that day, that there would be some "tomorrow," the next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did he say anything else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Aside from the people from Koritnik and Sase, are there other people present on the street at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No, not Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were there Serbs in the area at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: There were Serbs, but not women and children; just soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were you able to tell whether those soldiers were members of the Yugoslav People's Army or other types of soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Most of them were local Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you describe for us how they were dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: The majority were wearing multicoloured uniforms, predominantly green in colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Similar to the camouflage uniforms you've referred to already in your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were these people armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you and other members of the group left this area by the bridge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And approximately how long did you remain in this area before you left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Until half past 2.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And how was it you came to leave this area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: We were led by Mitar Vasiljevic to Nova Mahala.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did he say anything before what you describe as leading you to Nova Mahala?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes. He said, "There are no buses today. There will be some tomorrow."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you know where he was leading you before you left this area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Well, we were familiar with the streets of the neighbourhood, but we didn't know where he was taking us to.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe for us the path that you took from this area by the bridge to the place that you're describing as Nova Mahala?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Again, we went back via the Rzav bridge; that is, we passed by the MUP and went towards Mahala.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And is Pionirska Street in Mahala?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was Mitar Vasiljevic among the group of people that went up to Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And do you recall where he was in relation to the group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: He was walking ahead of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When you arrived at the Rzav River and crossed the bridge, did you see the people you described earlier as having a machine-gun? Did you see them at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you tell us how long it took to travel from the area by the bridge to the area known as Nova Mahala?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: About 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, can you describe to us what occurred once you arrived in the area of Nova Mahala?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: We entered the house of Jusuf Memic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And where was that house in relation to your school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: It's on the left side.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did all of the people enter the house of Jusuf Memic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No. Some got into the house of his son.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And where is that house in relation to the house of Jusuf Memic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Right across.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Across the street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Are these two houses on the same side of the street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And are they next to each other?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Which house did your mother initially go into?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: She got into his son's house, where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a -- I'm sorry. So the first house that you went into is which house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: His son's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And how long did you remain there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: For about an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, the group that came from Koritnik, did they all come up to this area in Nova Mahala?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And where was Mitar Vasiljevic at the time that you arrived in Nova Mahala?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: He was in front of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did he say anything that you could hear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, after an hour of being in the son's house, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: We got into Jusuf Memic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you tell us approximately how many people originally went into the son's house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: About ten.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did they all move out from that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us what happened when you moved to the house of Jusuf Memic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us what happened after you moved to the house of Jusuf Memic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Mitar Vasiljevic wrote something on a piece of paper. I personally didn't read what was written on that piece of paper, but he gave it to [redacted] and he kept this piece of paper which was supposed to protect us, allegedly, so that nobody would harm us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you know [redacted] before this day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us what village he was from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Sase.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did [redacted] tell the group of people what was contained on this paper?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you able -- you said that you couldn't read the paper. Were you able to see the paper?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes, we could see the paper. We saw the paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were you able to tell whether it was an official document or simply a piece of ordinary paper?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: It was just a piece of ordinary paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: After this occurred, did Mr. Vasiljevic remain at the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No. He left. I don't know where.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, can you describe the door -- where is the door on -- the entrance door on Jusuf Memic's house? Which side of the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: The door was on the upper part, because we were upstairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did that door face Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And the door of the other house, did that door face Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And which house is this that you're referring to now: the house of Jusuf Memic or the house of his son?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: The house of his son. In that house, the door was facing the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you have to take stairs to get up to the entrance door of that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And approximately how many steps to the entrance door of that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: I don't know. I couldn't tell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That afternoon, did you see anybody pass by the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did the people in the house have a meal that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And where did they get the food?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: What they had taken from their homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was anybody cooking with a fire that you could see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, after Mitar Vasiljevic left, did other people arrive at the house of Jusuf Memic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when other people entered the house, other Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you know a person by the name of "Milan Lukic"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when he arrived at the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Well, they arrived at half past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us, did you know Milan Lukic prior to this day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How did you know his name on this day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Probably because there were some people who had gone to school with him, men and women who knew him very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were there other people that came to the house with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe those people or tell us their names, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Milan Susnjar, also known as "Laco"; Milan Lukic; Sredoje Lukic; and Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The person you're describing as Sredoje Lukic, did you know him prior to this day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: I think he used to work as a police officer in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And the person you're describing as Milan Susnjar, did you know him prior to this day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Probably by sight, but not before this day. But there were people there who knew him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you learn his name from people that were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, before I proceed, this might be a good place to break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Very well. We'll adjourn now until 1.30 [sic]. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm sorry that I gave everybody a fright when I said, "We'll adjourn until 1.30." I'm glad you all stayed away until 2.30. Yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness 38. Before the break, you were describing for us a period of time when Mr. Lukic, Sredoje Lukic, Mitar Vasiljevic and Milan Susnjar came to the house of Jusuf Memic. I want you to orient us regarding time. Are you able to estimate how much time elapsed between the time that Mitar Vasiljevic left the house the first time and the time that these men arrived at the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Well, about an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And between the time that he left the first time and then returned with these men, did anybody else come to the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did anybody else pass the house, that you could see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, could you describe for us how Mr. Vasiljevic was dressed at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: He had a black hat and a black uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was it the same as when you saw him earlier in the day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And could you tell if he was armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And are you able to tell us what he was armed with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: An automatic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask you to describe each of the other men. Can you tell us what they were wearing? We'll begin with Mr. Lukic, Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: He was wearing a multicoloured uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what was the predominant colour of that uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Green.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was that a camouflage-type uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And could you tell if he was armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes. He also had an automatic weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. Sredoje Lukic, could you please describe what he was wearing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: The same as Milan Lukic. He was armed with an automatic weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And finally, Mr. Milan Susnjar, can you describe what he was wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: The same as Milan and Sredoje, and he had a bayonet.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is that the only weapon that he had with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Could you repeat that, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You said he had a bayonet. Was this the only weapon he had or did he have other weapons as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: He had an automatic rifle as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, aside from these four men, did you see any other people there present at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe for us what happened when these four men came to the house of Jusuf Memic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Mitar Vasiljevic and Milan Lukic were in front of the house, that is to say, where the windows were. He was on one side and the other one was on the other side. And Milan Susnjar and Sredoje were inside, and they were searching for money and gold. If you didn't give it up, then you would get a bullet in your forehead.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did one of the two men that was inside say something regarding money and gold?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No. They just asked us for money and gold.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us, using as best you're able their words, what was said to the people inside the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Milan Susnjar said, "Money and gold. If you don't give it up, you'll get a bullet in your forehead."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And the other person with him, Sredoje Lukic, I believe, did he say anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No. He was standing in the middle of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Are you able to approximate for us what time of the day this is occurring?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: About 5.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did any of these four men have any covering on their face or any disguise on their face?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe for us what occurred after Mr. Susnjar demanded this money from the people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: They searched us in the room next door. That is to say, they took our clothes off. We were naked, men and women.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: This other room that you're referring to, can you tell us what the room was used for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Probably for sleeping in.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you describe for us in greater detail how the people in the house were searched? Were they all searched together or in groups or individually?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Individually.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And who was inside that room, doing the search?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Milan Susnjar.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And where was the other person at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: He was in the neighbouring room.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, you said earlier in your testimony that you saw Milan Lukic and Mitar Vasiljevic at the front of the house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And how was it you were able to see them at the front of the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Well, we could see them -- I could see them when they came, all four of them, and then two of them went down outside in front of the house and the other two were inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And how were you able to see where they went outside the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Because I heard them talking. They said that we shouldn't throw any jewellery or money out of the window.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Approximately how long did it take for all of the people in the house to be searched? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: About two hours, I think, two and a half, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And during this entire two-hour period, is it Mr. Susnjar who is doing the actual searching of people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What happened after the last person was searched?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Then Milan Susnjar said, "We're going to drink now, have a drink."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Then what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Then they left. We stayed on there in the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when some of these men returned to the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you estimate for us the period of time between when they left after the search and the next time some of these men appeared at the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: I know they came at about half past 10.00, because I had a watch on my hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was that a watch that was not taken during the search?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And why was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Well, who had earrings in their ears and rings on their fingers, they didn't take that; just if you had anything on you, any other things on you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was it dark out at this point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: You mean when they came at half past 10.00 or when they searched us?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, when they came at half past 10.00.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes, it was dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe for us what happened when some of these people returned.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: They said, "The Green Berets are shooting. You have to hide in the cellar."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you able to see who it was that returned at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes; the same four men who had searched us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You've just described somebody as speaking. Did you see who or hear who it was that spoke?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No, I didn't see anything, but I heard who was doing the talking.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You heard who was doing the talking?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you able to identify who it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you give us the names of the people that returned at this point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Milan Susnjar, Mitar Vasiljevic, Sredoje Lukic, and Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was there any source or sources of light that you could tell at this point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes, there was some light there, and in the house next door there was no light.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So was there light in the house of Jusuf Memic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were there lights in the house of his son?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did any of these men have a source of light with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe it for us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: They had a flashlight.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How many of them had a flashlight?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: All four of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What happened after the man made this statement regarding the Green Berets; what happened after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: After that, they took us into the next house, Adem Omeragic's house, and they told us that we'd be safest in the cellar. And when we started going out of the house of Jusuf Memic, they said, "Fuck you."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When you say "they," are you able to be more specific about which of these men said that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No, I couldn't recognise that because it was night-time and we didn't dare look at them that much. We were afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: On the way to this other house, were you able to see any of these men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: All four of them took up positions between one house and the next, but I couldn't actually see where they were standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Are you familiar with a creek in the area of Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe for us where the Omeragic house is with respect to that creek?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: The creek is behind the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you enter the room of that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Which one do you mean? Adem Omeragic's?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Adem Omeragic's house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: It was just one room, actually, as far as I was able to understand. It was night-time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Approximately how far was the distance between the house of Jusuf Memic and the house of Adem Omeragic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: About 150 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to describe for the Chamber what the inside of that room looked like. What was its approximate size?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Perhaps eight by eight.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That's metres?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were there windows in that room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes. There were two windows.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And in which direction did those windows face?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: The lower side of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If one were to stand inside the house and look out the window, what would one be looking at?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: The creek flows below the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Would that be true for both windows? Were both windows on the same side of the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Aside from -- let me ask you this: Were there any stairs to the upper floors of this house which you could tell from the room that you were in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No, I couldn't see that because it was dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Aside from the two windows you've described and the door of this house, was there any way that you could see to enter or leave the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The windows in the house, did they have glass in them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And was there anything else, aside from the glass, on those windows?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes. There was a net of some kind, some netting.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you able to tell whether both windows had glass?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes, there was glass on both the windows.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were you able to tell whether both windows had this netting that you're describing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: I couldn't see that because I jumped up to the second window from the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe this netting with a little greater detail for the Court, perhaps by using an example of something similar to the netting that covered the window?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: The netting was -- oh, there were -- there were several nets from peppers, paprikas.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter notes: Probably from the sacks.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was the netting similar to the net sacks that peppers are sold in in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes, similar to that, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What, if any, furniture was in the room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: As far as I know, there was just a table.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Does your expertise, Mr. Groome, extend to the size of those nets that the paprikas are sold in in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Not mine, Your Honour, but I can certainly ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. Are they like a tennis court net or something?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'll ask a few more questions regarding that and see.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I want to ask a few more questions regarding the nets that you've described here. Did the netting cover the entire window that you described as being covered by it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes, it covered the whole window.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you approximate for us, what would be the open area in the net? How large were the holes or the open spaces in the net?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Perhaps half a centimetre.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Would those holes have been larger or smaller than the spaces that we would see in a tennis net?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Smaller, smaller.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Would the space of the net have been large enough to put your hand through it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No. Perhaps a mosquito could get by, but that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The other question, I suppose, which will arise is: What was it made of; plastic, or metal, or what?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you able to tell what material this netting was made from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: It's plastic, mostly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you able to tell -- let me ask this question: Was the netting on the inside of the glass or on the outside of the glass?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Aside from this table, was there any other furniture in the room, that you could tell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No, I couldn't tell because it was night, dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could you describe for us, where were you with respect to the people that went into this -- well, let me ask you this: How many people went into the room of this house? Can you estimate that for us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: About 75 to 80.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And where were you in that group; one of the first, one of the last, or in the middle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: I was in the middle, by the table.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were people standing in the room or was there anywhere to sit in the room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Some people were standing, others were sitting, but there wasn't enough room.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us what you observed when you went into the room? Were any of the four men you've described inside the room when you went into the room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No, nobody was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What did you do after you entered the room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: I went to sleep. I put my arm on the table and went to sleep. And suddenly I heard a scream and cries, and I heard someone say, "They are going to set light to us."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you able to tell who said that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: I couldn't say. I don't know who said that, but I just heard someone say it. It was a woman, a female voice.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could you tell where in the room this person was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: By the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you know how long you were asleep?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: I couldn't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us what happened after you heard the screams?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: I moved to the window, and I saw a woman breaking the window. It was VG18.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: I rushed to the window. She had managed to break part of the glass or part of the window, the one window pane, and I broke the other. And VG18 then got the netting down, and I tried to jump out. When I tried to jump out, the part by the door was in flames so that I was able to recognise Milan Susnjar standing there, standing next to the other window and door, and then he went off towards the next-door window. I came back into the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Then he threw a bomb in the next-door window by the door. The bomb exploded, and I jumped out.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Before you jumped out, did you see or smell smoke in that room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At what point in time did you first realise that there was smoke in the room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: When I wanted to try and jump out, it was suffocating.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe that smoke for us? Is there anything unusual about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: It was some sort of mat. I don't know what.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You said it was some sort of mat. Can you describe what you mean by that, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Mata [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe for us again the smoke and what you believe it came from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Well, it was some sort of mixture like paint, or dye, or something like that. It smelt like that. It was a blend of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time that you noticed a flame in that room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us when it was you first remember seeing flames in that room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: When I moved towards the window.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you tell us where in the room you saw flames?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: At the entrance door.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What were the other people in the room doing at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: They were screaming, crying.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At the time you first saw flames, is this before or after Milan Susnjar threw what you described as a bomb in one of the windows?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him at the time the fire broke out on the first window and I was about to jump, jump out, and the area -- one part of the area in front of the house was lit.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What was it lit from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: It had already been on fire before he threw it in.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The window that you jumped out of, was it the window closest to the door or furthest from the door?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Furthest from the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe for us what happened as you jumped out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: I hid in the bushes not far from the house, maybe 20, 25 metres away from it, and I was watching the house and fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where was your mother at the time that you first saw the flames break out inside the room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: I didn't know anything about what was going on with her at the time I jumped out.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where was she the last time you saw her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: We were together in the house, that is, in the house that was on fire. And then I never saw her again up until 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And when was it -- the last time you saw her in that house? At what point in time did you last see her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: I can't say exactly when that was because I was trying to get out.
