utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You spoke earlier about going to the window the first time and then coming back in. Was it before or after that event?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Before.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you recall her saying anything to you at the time that this person screamed that, "They are burning us," or, "They are going to burn us"? Did your mother say anything to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No, she didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you say anything to her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, can you be more precise -- I'll withdraw that. When you jumped outside the window of the house, was the house in flames at that point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did the light from those flames illuminate the area around the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you able to see anybody outside the house at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And where did you go immediately after you jumped out of the window of the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: I went behind the house. I was in a bush there, and it was from there that I watched the house burn and could hear people cry. There was shooting from automatic weapons as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe where you were in relation to the creek that runs behind the house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: I crossed over. I crossed the creek. There was a little bridge there that I crossed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And would you describe what the ground was like on the far side of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the creek; whether it was flat, whether there was a hill?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: There were some hills and houses around that area. It was a populated area where both Serbs and Muslims lived, Croats as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And you've described yourself as watching this fire. Approximately how far from the rear of this house are you at the point that you're watching this fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Twenty-five, maybe thirty metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Would you describe for us what you observed or -- sorry. Approximately how long did you stay there in that bush and watch the fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: For about half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you describe for us what you saw during that half an hour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: I listened to their screams. I could hear people cry, including women and children, and I could see the house in flames.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: During the time that you're watching this fire, did you think that your mother was still in the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you think that your mother burned to death in that house that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When was it that you found out that your mother had escaped the house that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So between 1992 and 1995, you believed that your mother had died on the 14th of June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I'm going to ask that the witness be shown a black and white copy of Exhibit 17.1, and I would ask that it be introduced as Prosecution Exhibit Number 17.1.38 to indicate that this witness will be making some marks on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Let's wait until he's marked it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Witness 38, I'm going to ask you to take the blue pen in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: We'll leave it on the desk and have the witness make the marks there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If you'll take the blue pen, I would ask you to put "VG38" at the bottom of that piece of paper to indicate that it's you that's making these marks.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask you to trace, with the blue marker, the path that the group from Koritnik took on its way from Koritnik down to the place by the bridge that you indicated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Has there been any dispute about this with any witness so far?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I'm going to ask him to mark one of the events that happened on that path. Does Your Honour wish us to move on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm not sure. Is there a dispute about this particular event that you want him to show? It's not something you have to do with every witness. There's been no dispute, so far as I have ascertained, to the description of how they arrived in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We don't really need to repeat that with every witness. That's the point about getting on with the case. If there is an event that there is no evidence about or you want to add to something, by all means, let's go straight to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Witness 38, I'd ask you to put "MV1" and a circle to indicate where it was you saw Mitar Vasiljevic the first time that day.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask you -- I'll have you make a few marks before we put it on the ELMO. I'd ask you to indicate where it was that this machine-gun was mounted on the car as you crossed the bridge.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now I'd ask you to take the red pen, and would you trace the route that you describe Mitar Vasiljevic as having led the group of people into the area known as "Nova Mahala."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At this time, I would ask that the usher place the exhibit on the ELMO. Your Honour, at this time I would tender 17.1 into evidence as 17.1.38.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Any objection, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. It will be Exhibit P17-1-VG38.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now I'd ask the witness be shown a black and white copy of Prosecution Number 17.3. I'd ask it be placed on the desk.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask you to take the red pen and put "VG38" to indicate that you're the person drawing on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask you to put a number "1" on the roof of the house that you're describing as Jusuf Memic's.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And I'd ask you to put an arrow to show us where the door is on that house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask you to put a "2" on the roof of the house that belongs to his son.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And an arrow to indicate where the door on that house is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And I'd ask you to put a "3" on the house that was ultimately set on fire.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And I'd ask you to put an arrow to indicate where the door is on that house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask you now to put an "MV2" to indicate where is the first place that you saw Mr. Vasiljevic up in this area on this day.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask you now to put "MV3" to indicate where Mr. Vasiljevic was the next time you saw him up in the Pionirska Street area.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And finally, I'd ask you to show us or trace in red the path that you took into the house from House Number 1 to House Number 3.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask that that now be placed on the ELMO. Your Honour, at this time I would tender 17.3 as 17.3.38 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I don't know why you do this for us if we can't see it. The other one didn't seem to have very much interest to it, but this one is important. I can see "1," I think I can see a "3." Perhaps we could use a pointer and then we'll see where this witness has made these marks.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I would ask the witness take the pointer. I would ask you to point to House Number 1.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now point to the house that you've marked as House Number 2.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And House Number 3.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where is the door on House Number 1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: In the area above.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And where is the door on House Number 2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Here, from the entrance from the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, can you point to where you've made the mark "MV2."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: In front of the door of the house of Jusuf Memic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And where did you make the mark "MV3"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I didn't mark it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. I would ask the document be placed on the desk again.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you need to make a correction to what you've done?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No, everything is okay. It is that "MV3" -- you told me about MV1 and MV2.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Point to -- where is the first place you saw Mitar Vasiljevic in this area of Visegrad on this day? Can you point to where that is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what number did you put in that, "MV" what? Without leaning over.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you point once again to the first place you saw Mitar Vasiljevic that day.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what have you written in there to indicate that?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where is the second place that you saw Mitar Vasiljevic that day? Can you point to that for us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what have you written there to indicate that?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now I'd ask you just to trace very slowly the path that you took from the house marked number "1" to the house marked number "3."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, at this time, I would re-tender that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Any objection, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Exhibit P17-3-VG38.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd now ask that Prosecution Number 17.7 be placed on the desk in front of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: VG38, I would ask you once again to write "VG38" at the bottom of that document.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And I'd ask you to circle the window that you testified you jumped out of.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And I'd ask that that be placed on the ELMO. Your Honour, at this time I would tender that into evidence as Prosecution 17.7.VG38.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Any objection, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. That will be Exhibit P17-7-VG38.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And finally I would ask that the Prosecution Document Number 17.14.VG38 be placed before the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And once again, I would ask the witness to write "VG38" at the bottom of that photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The place that you hid in the bush and watched the fire, is that on this photograph or can you find it on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask you to put a circle and put "VG38" inside that circle to indicate for us where it was you hid and watched the fire from.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And I would now ask that that be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I would ask you to take the pointer and indicate for us where you have made the mark.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And I would ask you now to point to the house that was set on fire.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, I would like to tender that into evidence as Prosecution Exhibit 17.14.VG38.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Any objection, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. That will be Exhibit P17-14-VG38.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I have no further questions. Thank you, VG38.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. VG38, at the relevant times, you said you were about [redacted]; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You attended the primary school in [redacted]?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Only that particular year or had you attended that school even before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: From the [redacted] [redacted].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Sir, when you are dealing with questions coming from your left, from Mr. Domazet there, you are both speaking the same language. Both the questions and the answers have to be interpreted into English and into French. The interpreters have a great deal of difficulty if you don't pause before you start your answer because they are still interpreting the question. So just wait a few seconds before you answer the question, just as Mr. Domazet will be waiting an appreciable time before he starts the question. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So that year, you were in the [redacted]?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: In your school or in your class, were there both Muslim and Serb students or was only one community represented?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: There were both Muslims and Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: During that particular school year in 1992, was the situation any different from previous years or was it the case that some of your colleagues had already left the school? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you remember the reason why? And who was it that left; Serbs, or Muslims, or both?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Muslims were the first ones to leave, and later on, I don't know about the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Some 15 days before the Uzice Corps entered Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Just one moment. We never got an interpretation of your question. If you tell us what your question was, it will help us to understand the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "When did this happen? When did the majority of students leave school?" That was my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you, sir, leave school then too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And from that time on, you were in your village, Koritnik; is that right or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes, I was in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you talked about leaving the village -- actually, prior to leaving the village, asked by Mr. Groome what happened on the 13th of June, you said that some Serbs came to the village and that this was a question that was discussed. How do you know that it was the 13th of June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Well, I won't forget the 13th and 14th for as long as I live.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, I can well believe that. I know you have every reason to remember those dates. But I'm asking you: How come you remembered that it was the 13th the day before and the 14th the day after, and the time you left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Can you repeat that, please? I don't follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet, it might be simpler if you look at it from this point of view: Even if he was told later what the date was, it doesn't matter, does it? Is the point you're trying to ask him: Was it only the day before that he left, the day before the fire?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: May I suggest you approach it from that point of view, because the question is confusing, if I may say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I'm asking, because in the statement you gave to the investigator -- and you were interviewed by the investigators of this Tribunal; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: In that statement, you say up until the 14th of June, you were hiding in the village, and that a day later you moved to Visegrad, which is a little different from what you said today. And that's why I asked you what the date was or whether you were able to remember the date on the basis of something or, as Judge Hunt said, somebody perhaps told you that date later on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No, sir. The date, the 13th, was when we left the village, and the 14th -- that is to say, we were in the village on the 13th, and on the 14th we were set fire to.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And you're sure that was the 14th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you perhaps remember what day of the week that 14th was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: It was Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you spoke about what went on before that at the stadium, that was quite a bit before that date, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes. It was in April. Whether it was the 16th or not, 15th or 16th, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Was it an occasion when a large number of inhabitants were gathered together, they had come from all parts, and some of the JNA -- a JNA officer held a speech, addressed them, and said that they should all return to Visegrad; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes, I remember Jovanovic making a speech, saying that all Muslims should return to Visegrad because, as he put it, allegedly they could live safely there. But when they went back, that was the worst time in Visegrad, the worst killings.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you say "the worst killings in Visegrad," are you referring to the period when the JNA was in Visegrad or after the JNA had left Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No, after the Uzice Corps had left, and this was -- the perpetrators were the local Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you remember what happened after that meeting/rally at the stadium? You said today that at the Drina Hotel at the stadium itself, that you went there. Is that a hotel or is it something else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: It's a hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You said today that you stayed in that hotel for 15 days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You told the investigator of the OTP that on the following day, the day after, that is, that you were taken, accompanied by the Uzice Corps soldiers, to the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No, that's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: It says so in your statement. But you claim that that's not correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No, sir. Some returned, others stayed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: The ones that stayed at the stadium - and you were among them - did they stay of their own free will or were they kept there by the JNA, the army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No, sir. They were not safe where they lived in the surrounding villages around Visegrad, and that's why they didn't dare go back.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes. So that's why they stayed of their own free will. Nobody was compelled to stay, was forced to stay?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you spoke about your journey from the village to Visegrad, you mentioned that three buses -- as many as three buses passed by you, and you identified the people as being the inhabitants from Vlahovici village. How do you know they were from Vlahovici village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: As far as I was able to understand, the buses didn't stop at all. Yes, a woman got on - she was almost 90 - and she went off with these other people. She was from the village of Vlahovici, and she's still alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So a bus stopped for this woman to get on, and that's when you learnt that the people were from Vlahovici; is that right? Have I Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. understood you correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: In Sase, you were joined, as you said, by about 10 to 13 people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You said that you knew one of these individuals. Did you know the others and, if so, how long had you known them for and how did you come to know them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: I knew one person, and I knew another person, too, because it was a relative of mine. We were related.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You reached Visegrad sometime after 12.00, you say that it was about 12.30 or thereabouts, and you came to in front of the hotel. You said that Milorad Lipovac came to the hotel with you and that he stepped aside to talk to Mitar Vasiljevic for about ten minutes; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Was that straight after you arrived at the hotel? Was Lipovac the first person to approach that man, the one you identified as being Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Were you able to hear their conversation? Did you hear what they were talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did Lipovac leave after that? Did you see him at all after his coming to in front of the hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No, I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did Lipovac say anything, tell you anything before he left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you described the person you say you identified as Mitar Vasiljevic, you said that he had a black hat and a black uniform on. That's what you said today.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What do you mean by "a black uniform"? Because I myself don't know that uniforms like that existed, if you're referring to a military uniform.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: It was a military uniform, but I don't know what it actually represented.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So you think it was a military uniform and the colour was black?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you happen to remember what he had on his feet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What about the other people who were there, the Serb policemen, if they were there? Did they say where you ought to go and was Bikavac mentioned as a possible location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No, Bikavac wasn't mentioned; just Nova Mahala, the New Mahala.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you say "Nova Mahala," can you explain to the Court what you mean? Which part of Visegrad was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: It's a settlement called Mahala and it's actually Pionirska Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Isn't the Mahala settlement a settlement below Pionirska Street? The part up until the beginning of Pionirska Street, isn't that what they call Mahala?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Could you repeat that, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Isn't Mahala part of Visegrad which is below Pionirska Street, where Pionirska Street begins, next to the Cadjava cafe, that part of Visegrad, and not the upper part, which is Pionirska street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: I couldn't really answer that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Asked by Mr. Groome about the new hotel and the distance from the old bridge, I think you said that you couldn't determine that distance because you were much younger then and didn't know. I think you said something like that. Does that mean that you didn't go into that part of town often for you to be able to tell us now the details of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: I think it's by the bridge, that the hotel is by the bridge. And I went around Visegrad enough, because I went to school there, so I knew it sufficiently well. I didn't actually know the streets and their names very well, but I knew the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Is there anything that lies between the bridge and the hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes. There's a garden.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Is there anything opposite the gardens?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: There's a monument to a writer, Ivo Andric.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did it exist -- did the monument exist while you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I don't actually know whether it did or didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you went towards the Mahala or Pionirska Street, we have established the direction you took. You said today that Mitar Vasiljevic accompanied the column; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Mitar Vasiljevic did go with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did anybody else accompany the column, of the people who were not of the column, who were not from Visegrad and Sase?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No. There was just Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So only he accompanied you and went from the hotel to the Memic house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you reached Memic's house, you said that Mitar Vasiljevic wrote something down on an ordinary piece of paper which you couldn't see or read. Did you happen to see the writing itself or did you just hear about the existence of a piece of paper?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: I saw him when he was writing it down, but I didn't know what he was writing down. And he gave the piece of paper to [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Where did this happen? Where did this take place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: In front of Jusuf Memic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Who did you see? Who was present there when he wrote this down?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: [redacted] was present.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So the two of them, [redacted] and Mitar Vasiljevic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: How far were they from you and the others?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: The other people were in the house, and we were separated some 10 to 15 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Were the two of them standing or were they sitting down?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: They were standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you happen to notice how long they were standing and talking and whether that was the only place they stood and talked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: I can't really say how long they were standing there for and talking. I don't know. I simply don't know. All I do know is that they were talking and he wrote on this piece of paper. And what he wrote was: "If anybody comes to touch you, just show them the piece of paper."

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you happen to notice them doing anything else apart from talking and this person writing down on a piece of paper?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you happen to notice a bottle in either of these persons' hands? Were they drinking anything from a bottle perhaps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: (redacted) was an alcoholic. Probably they were -- he gave him some brandy to drink.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So as far as you remember, they were drinking something, but I'm sure you didn't pay much attention to that; is that right? A Yes, that's right. Q Did this conversation with (redacted) take place immediately after your arrival and after you were put up in the Memic house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You can't remember how much time went by from the time you arrived to the time you saw them, the two of them talking?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No, I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you see them separate after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No. I went into the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did [redacted] go into the house later as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Without Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: That's right, without Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: From that moment on, did you see Mitar Vasiljevic at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you remember anything else that would have been characteristic that you would remember, any other event that took place before you went into the house which would catch your attention in any way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Well, yes. In the meantime, a woman went out to look into the house at that Mahala place, and she found two people slaughtered there, with their throats slit, from Koritnik, and we knew who they were and what they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So that was in the house where you -- I'm asking you about the house where you were. Did anybody come and take anybody away from that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Who, and what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Mitar Vasiljevic was outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You're now talking about the other event when you say that the four men turned up; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: But I'm referring to before that. Did anybody come before that and take any other people out of the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What about the people you said were found in this other house? And if I understood you, you said they had been slaughtered, their throats slit.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: It was a married couple; they had been found with their throats slit. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No, they weren't a married couple. It was an elderly man and an elderly woman.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you know who they were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can you tell us their names or surnames?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Seco Kurspahic and Rasema Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I'd like now to ask you about the second event, focus on the second event, when you saw Mitar Vasiljevic for the second time, when you say that four men turned up and you gave us their names: Milan Lukic; Sredoje Lukic; Milan Susnjar, nicknamed Laco; and Mitar Vasiljevic. Is that right; they were the four men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: As we have descriptions of these men by witnesses, and apart from Milan, who most people know on the basis of some other characteristics, they spoke about a tall, fair man in the group. Who would you say was this tall, fair or blond person, a tall, fair guy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No, he wasn't tall and fair, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Of those four men, none of them you would describe as tall and fair; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did anybody have a moustache?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: Yes. It was Milan Susnjar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And was there someone who was very young, a young person of 18, 19?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No. As far as I was able to see, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: There was nobody like that amongst those four men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: No, sir, I didn't see anybody like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Could you -- you explained to us how you knew the names of those men, and you said that you knew some of them. Now, at that time, straight away, immediately, while they were there, did you know their names, or did you learn of their names later on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: There were people there who knew all four of them, and that's when we learnt their names, when they took the money and gold, whereas they knew Mitar, some of them knew Mitar from before, Milan Lukic, that is. They knew him from before. Milan Susnjar as well, Laco, from the village, and Sredoje.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: The people who knew Susnjar, what did they say? Who and what was he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38
utterances.text: As far as I heard, he was a baker.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet, this is going to be a long subject, I think, and it's now 4.00. So we'll adjourn - I hope I get it right this time - until 9.30 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 2nd day of October, 2001, at 9.30 a.m. 24 25
